newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends marginally down against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends marginally down against dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended a quiet Friday at 35.845/855 per dollar, down from the opening quotes of 35.825/845 but off the day's low of 35.865, dealers said.
They said good dollar supplies kept the rupee steady through the day till some late demand from a large state-run bank from eastern India pushed it down briefly.

"There was some demand in the morning from corporates and interbank short-covering," said a dealer. "Then dollar supplies came in and the rupee was steady for a long while before dollar demand from the state-run bank came in the late afternoon."
The rupee traded on Friday at a high of 35.845 and a low of 35.865, he said.
Dealers said premia on forward dollars fell on prospects of improving domestic liquidity.

The Reserve Bank of India said on Thursday that banks' cash reserve ratio requirements would be cut by one percentage point to 10 percent in January. This would be done through two cuts of 50 basis points each on January 4 and January 18.
It said banks' resources would be augmented by 42.75 billion rupees as a result of the cuts.
Dealers said the premia on six-month dollars ended Friday at an annualised 7.42 percent from Thursday's close of 8.1 percent.
